```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

SEARS 2.0 allows a model to be useful for early screening without granting it a permanent final veto.

```{r}
library(SEARS2)
sears2_authority("sears2", direct_mature = FALSE, overlapping = TRUE, model_qualified = TRUE)
sears2_authority("sears2", direct_mature = TRUE, overlapping = TRUE, model_qualified = TRUE)
sears2_authority("static_model", direct_mature = TRUE, overlapping = TRUE, model_qualified = TRUE)
```

## Same direct data, different final authority

```{r}
common <- list(
  activity_successes = c(D2 = 18, D3 = 18),
  activity_n = c(D2 = 36, D3 = 36),
  tolerability_failures = c(D2 = 4, D3 = 14),
  tolerability_n = c(D2 = 36, D3 = 36),
  hard_admissible = c(D2 = TRUE, D3 = TRUE),
  model_activity = c(D2 = 0.30, D3 = 0.60)
)
do.call(sears2_analyze, c(list(strategy = "static_model"), common))
do.call(sears2_analyze, c(list(strategy = "sears2"), common))
```

In the primary SEARS 2.0 implementation, post-maturity `Support` is contextual rather than quantitative:
it does not alter the randomized likelihood, dominance probabilities, or final eligibility set.
